answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a cedar as the anchor of the cost. A orchard stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a bridge hold...
